inventory.visualPurpose: T- and B-cell activation — the two two-signal diagrams
inventory.sourceFigureDescription: Two side-by-side vector diagrams. Left (T-cell activation): an Antigen-presenting cell (Antigen on MHC II/I) faces a Naïve T cell (T cell receptor, CD4/8); signal 1 = antigen-MHC to TCR; signal 2 = CD80/86 (B7) on the APC to CD28 on the naïve T cell; output box 'Activated T cell actions'. Right (B-cell activation and class switching): an Activated CD4+ T cell (T cell receptor, CD4, CD40L) faces a B cell (B cell receptor, MHC II with Antigen, CD40); signal 1 = antigen-MHC II to TCR; signal 2 = CD40L to CD40; Cytokines arrow from the Th cell direct class switching; output box 'Activated B cell actions'.

notes: Census: the two activation diagrams are pure vector (pdf 123 rasters = two 1x1 pixel artifacts only) — both are conveyed in ONE original KYP schematic (activation-signal-model) covering both signal-pair routes plus the anergy/peripheral-tolerance strip; the verbatim activation sequences are the note's table block. No E27 content (pdf 124) claimed.
